headline.headline: KAT PLAYS THROUGH GRIEF AS KNICKS TOP SPURS IN GAME 1
headline.deck: Towns honors late mother with emotional performance in NBA Finals opener
headline.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns carried more than a basketball Wednesday night in San Antonio. One day after the death of his mother, the New York Knicks center took the floor for Game 1 of the NBA Finals and helped power New York past the Spurs, 105-95, in a performance that left the basketball world searching for words.

Jalen Brunson and the Knicks steadied themselves after falling behind by as many as 14 points, surging late to seize control of the series opener. The victory gave New York the home-court advantage and momentum heading into Game 2, with the Knicks demonstrating the kind of collective resolve that has defined their postseason run through the Eastern Conference.

After the final buzzer, Towns paused at center court and looked skyward, visibly overcome with emotion as teammates surrounded him. The Spurs, playing in their first Finals appearance in years, found no answer for New York's fourth-quarter push, and the Knicks now hold a 1-0 series lead with the next game set for this weekend.

secondary.headline: GOLDEN KNIGHTS SEIZE EDGE AS HURRICANES HUNT FOR OFFENSE
secondary.deck: Vegas grabs Game 1 win while Carolina's top line goes cold at the worst time
secondary.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights enter the Stanley Cup Final as the team to beat after claiming Game 1 against the Carolina Hurricanes, establishing themselves as the new odds-on favorites for the championship. Carolina's top line, which carried the Hurricanes through two rounds of playoff hockey, went quiet at the precise moment the stakes were highest.

Hurricanes coaches acknowledged after the game that more production from their premier forwards is not optional — it is essential. Vegas has historically made life miserable for opposing offenses in the postseason, and the Hurricanes will need to find answers quickly before the series slips further from their grasp.

secondary.headline: MARLINS SILENCE NATIONALS BATS, RIDE LATE RUNS TO 4-1 WIN
secondary.deck: Miami scores three times over final two innings to pull away in Washington
secondary.body:
The Miami Marlins turned a tight pitchers' duel into a comfortable victory Wednesday night, plating two runs in the eighth inning and one more in the ninth to beat the Washington Nationals, 4-1, before 16,695 at Nationals Park. Alvarez earned the win on the mound as Miami held Washington scoreless over the final six frames after the Nationals briefly knotted the score at one in the third.

Dylan Crews was hit by a pitch from Fairbanks in a game that took three hours and 13 minutes to complete. The Marlins, who managed their lone run through seven innings by plating one in the second, broke the game open with a two-run eighth before tacking on an insurance run in the ninth to secure the final margin.

secondary.headline: STEELERS LOCK UP WASHINGTON AS KITTLE EYES WEEK 1 RETURN
secondary.deck: Pittsburgh signs tight end to $42 million extension while San Francisco's Kittle recovers from torn Achilles
secondary.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers moved aggressively in the offseason market Wednesday, reaching agreement with tight end Darnell Washington on a four-year, $42 million extension that keeps one of the NFL's most physically imposing blockers in black and gold for the foreseeable future. Washington, who emerged as a key piece of Pittsburgh's offense, rewarded the team's faith with a deal that signals long-term commitment on both sides.

Meanwhile in Santa Clara, San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle offered an optimistic update on his recovery from a torn right Achilles, telling reporters he is ahead of schedule and fully expects to be ready for Week 1 of the 2026 season. Kittle called himself "on track" and said the rehabilitation process has gone better than anticipated, welcome news for a Niners offense that missed him dearly.

column.headline: TOWNS SHOWED US WHAT SPORT IS REALLY FOR
column.body:
There are nights in sports that remind you why any of this matters. Karl-Anthony Towns lost his mother and then laced up his sneakers and played in the NBA Finals. Not because a contract forced him to. Not because a coach pressured him. But because sometimes the only language grief understands is the one you have spoken your whole life. Towns spoke it Wednesday night in San Antonio, and every person in that arena knew they were watching something far larger than basketball.

The Golden State Warriors used to talk about joy as a competitive weapon. Towns showed something deeper. He showed that love, real love, can get you off the floor when nothing else can. Whatever happens the rest of this Finals series, Game 1 already belongs to him. The Spurs can have the statistics. Towns earned everything else.

story.headline: GUARDIANS CLIP YANKEES IN BRONX AS RAMÍREZ, MANZARDO GO DEEP IN 5-4 THRILLER
story.deck: Cleveland rallies in eighth to edge New York, hand Yankees a painful home loss
story.body:
NEW YORK — José Ramírez homered for the second time in as many nights and Kyle Manzardo added a solo shot as the Cleveland Guardians held off the New York Yankees, 5-4, Wednesday at Yankee Stadium before 37,683 fans. The Guardians scored the decisive run in the eighth inning to take a 5-3 lead, then survived a Yankees rally in the ninth that pulled New York within one before Cleveland closer Smith, C., slammed the door.

Ramírez, who now has nine home runs on the season, also stole a base and drove the Guardians offense from the top of the order. Manzardo went deep for the seventh time in 2026, finishing with a double as well. For New York, Rhys Hoskins and Aaron Judge — credited in the notes as Jr. — each contributed home runs, with Hoskins reaching six on the year and Judge seven, but the Yankees stranded seven runners and could not complete the comeback. Paul Goldschmidt added a double in a losing cause.

The Guardians built their margin with crooked numbers in the second, fourth, sixth, and eighth innings, never allowing New York to take the lead. Winners were credited to Williams, G., and Smith, C., reflecting Cleveland's bullpen depth. The loss drops New York to a frustrating home defeat in a game they led briefly, tied multiple times, and ultimately could not win despite Judge's latest long ball lighting up the Stadium crowd.

story.headline: BRUNSON, KNICKS RALLY FROM 14 DOWN TO STUN SPURS IN GAME 1
story.deck: New York erases second-half deficit, takes series lead in San Antonio
story.body:
SAN ANTONIO — Jalen Brunson scored 30 points and led a furious late surge as the New York Knicks erased a 14-point second-half deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 105-95 in Game 1 of the NBA Finals on Wednesday night at the AT&T Center. The Knicks, playing as the road team, refused to fold under pressure and ripped off a decisive run in the final quarter to seize control of the series opener on enemy ground.

The Spurs held a commanding advantage through much of the second half, but Brunson steadily chipped away at the lead, attacking the rim and converting at the free-throw line with the game on the line. Karl-Anthony Towns contributed on both ends as New York's second unit kept the deficit manageable before Brunson's late heroics finally broke San Antonio's resolve. 'We know we have each other's backs,' Brunson said afterward, summing up the Knicks' gritty collective effort.

The win carried emotional weight beyond the final score. Towns, who lost his mother to illness in recent years, honored her memory following the victory, a moment that resonated deeply inside the Knicks locker room. New York will look to build on the momentum when Game 2 tips off in San Antonio later this week, with Brunson firmly established as the driving force of a Knicks team that now stands one win closer to a championship that has eluded the franchise for more than five decades.

story.headline: COOPER WINS JACK ADAMS AS GOLDEN KNIGHTS GRAB UPPER HAND IN STANLEY CUP FINAL
story.deck: Vegas takes Game 1 edge while Carolina's top line searches for answers
story.body:
Jon Cooper collected the Jack Adams Award on Thursday, cementing a legacy 14 seasons in the making in Tampa Bay. The Lightning bench boss, who guided the franchise to back-to-back Stanley Cup championships in 2020 and 2021, became one of the most decorated coaches in NHL history with the honor, recognized for his ability to sustain excellence long after most championship windows slam shut.

Meanwhile, the 2026 Stanley Cup Final has taken an early turn toward Las Vegas after the Golden Knights claimed a Game 1 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes, vaulting Vegas to the top of the championship odds boards. The Hurricanes, who entered the series as favorites, now face a familiar pressure: their top line has not generated the offensive production the organization needs to win four rounds against a Golden Knights squad built on depth and goaltending.

Carolina's brass acknowledged Thursday that more must come from their premier forwards if the Hurricanes hope to avoid falling into an early series hole. Vegas, a franchise that reached the Stanley Cup Final in its very first season back in 2018, has developed into a battle-tested postseason machine. The Hurricanes will look to respond when the series continues, but with Cooper earning his hardware and the Golden Knights riding momentum, the hockey world is watching Raleigh's next move very closely.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS SHUFFLE ACROSS THE LEAGUE AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are banking on new signal-callers to reverse their fortunes this fall.
story.body:
The quarterback carousel has spun wildly this offseason, reshaping the NFL landscape just months after the Philadelphia Eagles hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at Super Bowl LX. At least five teams have installed new starters under center since February, with veteran journeymen and promising young arms alike landing in unfamiliar cities ahead of what promises to be a dramatically altered 2026 season.

Among the most scrutinized moves, the Las Vegas Raiders signed former starter Justin Fields to a two-year deal worth $48 million, betting the athletic signal-caller can thrive under new head coach Mike Vrabel's system after Fields spent last season backing up in Pittsburgh. Meanwhile, the Cleveland Browns, desperate to end years of dysfunction, acquired veteran Sam Darnold from Minnesota in a trade that sent a second-round pick and a depth linebacker north to the Vikings, giving Cleveland its third starting quarterback in as many years.

The NFL Draft in late April added further intrigue, as three quarterbacks were selected in the first round, including Heisman Trophy winner Jalen Milroe, who slid to the New York Giants at pick seven after a string of surprising trades reshuffled the top of the board. General managers across the league now have until late July, when training camps open, to convince their fanbases that this time, finally, they have found their answers at the most important position in professional sports.
